papers.title_en: MAC-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Collaboration via Interconnected Tasks
papers.authors: Zerui Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Qichuan Liu, Zhishang Xiang, Zhimin Wei, Yunbo Tang, Zhuo Li, Jinsong Su, Zhihong Zhang
papers.evidence: 评估LLM多智能体协作的基准
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体系统评测常偏重任务难度，协作要求不足或仅覆盖预设协作模式。MAC-Bench将协作需求嵌入任务依赖与共享资源约束，并从基准任务中挖掘局部交互模式与全局任务结构，经粗到细组合生成互联任务图。任务在可执行环境中实例化，支持部分进展与完整解决的自动验证。该基准为多智能体协作能力提供了更系统、可复现的评测方式。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) tackle challenging tasks by dividing work among agents and coordinating their contributions toward shared objectives. Evaluating these systems therefore requires benchmarks that assess not only task-solving performance but also the ability to handle interdependent work. However, existing benchmarks often emphasize task difficulty without substantial collaboration requirements or evaluate only a limited range of predefined collaboration patterns. In this paper, we introduce MAC-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multi-agent collaboration through interconnected tasks. Rather than imposing predefined agent roles or communication protocols, MAC-Bench embeds collaboration requirements directly into task dependencies and shared-resource constraints. Specifically, we mine reusable collaboration structures from selected benchmark tasks at two levels. Local collaboration patterns capture recurring interactions among subtasks, while global task structures characterize how these interactions contribute to complete workflows. Through coarse-to-fine composition, these structures are recombined into task graphs combining different collaboration requirements. Tasks are instantiated in executable environments with automated verification of partial progress and complete task resolution.

papers.title_en: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
papers.authors: Zhihua Wang, Yunhao Feng, Yifeng Gao, Rui Pan, Baiheng Zhao, Zixing Chen, Xingjun Ma
papers.evidence: 评估持久记忆自主智能体的基准
papers.tldr: 记忆持久化AI智能体可跨会话保留指令，但恶意内容可能被写入记忆并在后续正常任务中持续影响决策。MemHarmBench以受害者为中心，覆盖用户、工作区/项目所有者和外部利益相关者三类对象，先注入并检验记忆留存，再移除攻击内容、开启保留记忆的新会话执行合法任务。实验发现跨会话攻击可保持行为隐蔽：智能体正常完成任务且无明显异常，却仍按攻击者意图做出关键决策。该基准把恶意记忆留存与下游决策及受影响方连接起来，揭示传统指标易忽略的安全风险。
papers.abstract_en: AI agents often rely on persistent memory to retain user preferences and operational rules across sessions. However, this capability introduces a new safety risk: malicious instructions from messages, documents, or Web content can be retained in memory and influence future tasks even after the original attack content is removed. Existing attack success metrics, however, fail to capture who is affected and how attacks translate into downstream harm during otherwise normal task execution. We introduce MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark for evaluating cross-session prompt injection in memory-persistent AI agents. MemHarmBench considers three categories of potential victims: users, workspace/project owners, and external stakeholders. Our evaluation first exposes an agent to malicious instructions and tests whether they are retained in memory. We then remove the attack content and initiate a new session with a legitimate task while preserving the agent's memory. We jointly evaluate whether the agent follows the attacker's intent, completes the legitimate task, and exhibits observable execution anomalies. Across multiple agent systems, we find that cross-session attacks can remain behaviorally stealthy: agents often complete tasks normally and exhibit no detectable anomalies while still making critical decisions aligned with the attacker's intent. By connecting malicious memory retention to downstream decisions and affected parties, MemHarmBench provides a systematic framework for exposing safety risks that conventional attack- and task-success metrics may overlook. We publicly release MemHarmBench at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/MemHarmBench.

papers.title_en: MV-IVF: Multi-Vector Retrieval via Multi-Vector Clustering
papers.authors: Kishen N Gowda, Laxman Dhulipala, Lars Gottesbüren, Rajesh Jayaram
papers.evidence: 面向近似检索的IVF式向量索引
papers.tldr: 多向量检索通过细粒度集合交互提升相关性，但搜索开销显著高于单向量。MV-IVF直接在多向量数据上构建原生IVF索引，并以MV-Lloyd按Chamfer目标聚类点云，形成分层树。查询时用best-first beam search定位叶簇，再对文档评分，并结合量化与批处理加速。在BEIR和LoTTE上取得更优延迟-召回权衡，90% Recall-10@10下延迟最多降8.03倍、QPS最多升173.5倍，证明原生IVF式多向量检索可行且高效。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-vector retrieval represents each query and document as a set of embeddings and scores relevance via fine-grained set-to-set interactions such as MaxSim (Chamfer similarity). This expressiveness improves retrieval quality over single-vector representations, but makes search substantially more expensive. Existing systems address this challenge primarily through proxy representations or filter-and-rerank pipelines that reduce candidate generation to single-vector search. We study the complementary direction of building a native IVF-style index directly over multi-vector data.   We introduce MV-IVF, an inverted-file index for multi-vector retrieval built on MV-Lloyd, a new Lloyd-style algorithm for clustering point clouds under a Chamfer objective. Our key observation is that once point clouds are assigned to clusters, the center-update step reduces to standard single-vector clustering over the flattened embeddings in each cluster. This enables efficient construction of a hierarchical IVF tree with center point clouds at internal nodes.   At query time, MV-IVF performs best-first beam search over the tree to identify promising leaf clusters, then scores the documents in those leaves. We further accelerate search using low-bit quantization, query compression, and cache-efficient batched search. We implement MV-IVF in MVSIC, an optimized C++ library and unified evaluation framework for multi-vector retrieval that includes several major approaches. Across BEIR and LoTTE text retrieval benchmarks, MV-IVF achieves strong latency--recall tradeoffs, the best batched throughput frontiers, and favorable build-time and index-size profiles. At $90\%$ Recall-$10$@$10$, MV-IVF achieves up to $8.03\times$ lower single-query latency and up to $173.5\times$ higher QPS than the baselines, demonstrating that native IVF-style indexing is practical and effective for scalable multi-vector retrieval.

papers.title_en: TRIO: Task Refinement with Individual Optimization for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.authors: Yingtao Ren, Xiao Luo, Yiwei Fu, Jinzhao Zhou, Yu-Cheng Chang, Chin-Teng Lin
papers.evidence: 多智能体迭代精炼的检索增强生成
papers.tldr: 现有RAG常因检索不充分和潜在幻觉而效果受限。TRIO将查询扩展、充分性判断与答案生成三个智能体组织为迭代细化框架，并分别用答案质量奖励、一致性投票标注和动态匹配奖励加课程学习进行个体优化。多基准实验表明其优于现有方法，能提升检索质量、证据利用与回答准确性。该工作为RAG的多智能体协同、查询细化和分目标优化提供了有效方案，并开源代码便于复现。
papers.abstract_en: This paper studies retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), which leverages external knowledge to improve the performance of language models. Despite the remarkable progress, current RAG approaches are still far from satisfactory due to inadequate retrieval and potential hallucinations. Towards this end, we propose a novel approach named Task Refinement with Individual Optimization (TRIO) for RAG. The core idea of our TRIO is to equip three well-designed agents with an iterative refinement paradigm by aligning their individual optimization objectives. Specifically, we first expand ambiguous queries with a query extension agent and quantify the reward based on the improved answer quality, which can be utilized to refine our agent for higher expansion efficiency. To enhance the retrieval quality, we include a unanimity voting to annotate the expanded query as insufficient or sufficient, and their generative outcomes are utilized as ground truth to optimize the judge agent. To further improve evidence utilization and answer accuracy, an answer agent is optimized with dynamic matching-based rewards with curriculum learning for final outputs. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark datasets validate the effectiveness of the proposed TRIO in comparison with state-of-the-art approaches. Our code is available at https://github.com/yingtaoren/TRIO.

papers.title_en: Toward Knowledge-Centric AI: Discovering, Internalizing, and Using Explicit Knowledge Across Agents and Generations
papers.authors: Yisen Gao, Haoyu Huang, Zhongwei Xie, Yufei Li, Hong Ting Tsang, Boyi Zhang, Qiao Xiao, Tianshi Zheng, Jiaxin Bai, Yangqiu Song
papers.evidence: 面向智能体长期记忆的显式知识层
papers.tldr: 当前AI智能体各自学习，知识被困在参数、上下文或系统专属记忆中，难以跨智能体与代际积累。作者主张构建独立于单一智能体的显式、持续演化知识层，让智能体发现知识，由该层将碎片化异构记录与经验内化为可组合、可修正的理解，再供跨系统跨代智能体使用并回传新结果。发现与使用已随大模型智能体快速发展，内化仍是瓶颈；应把内化作为持续训练与维护对象，并发展知识基础模型，以支撑复用、降本、可审计与代际连续性。
papers.abstract_en: Knowledge is how understanding accumulates across people and generations: durable records that outlive their producers and that others can check, combine, teach, and correct. AI agents are now built and run by many independent users and organizations, and each agent is upgraded, replaced, or retired within months. Yet what an agent learns stays trapped in model parameters, a transient context window, or a system-specific memory store that is appended to and retrieved from rather than processed. We argue that the next generation of AI should be knowledge-centric, built around an explicit, continuously evolving knowledge layer independent of any single agent. In this loop, agents discover knowledge from their environments and trajectories; the layer internalizes it by turning fragmented, heterogeneous records and experience into composable, revisable understanding; and agents across systems and generations use the result and return new outcomes for revision. While discovery and use have advanced rapidly with large language model agents, internalization remains the bottleneck. We argue that internalization should become a persistent object of training and maintenance-centered on condition-preserving conceptualization of events and deductive, inductive, and abductive reasoning across noisy, heterogeneous representations (text, tables, graphs, rules, and programs). To power this layer, we call for knowledge foundation models that provide shared neural capacity for knowledge computation, and outline a research agenda showing how an explicit knowledge layer delivers reuse, cost efficiency, auditability, and continuity across agent generations.

papers.title_en: Do Agents Still Follow the Rules? Benchmarking Rule Compliance under Agent Context Compaction
papers.authors: Yiwei Zha, Qingyu Meng, Herbert Bos, Min Chen
papers.evidence: 评估上下文压缩后智能体规则遵循的基准
papers.tldr: LLM智能体为适配上下文窗口会压缩长历史，但压缩后的上下文仍需保留约束后续动作的规则。作者构建基于开源pi harness的可配置基准ARCBench，在真实工具调用循环中按执行动作衡量规则遵循，并追踪压缩后违规来源。结果显示违规多发生在规则仍在压缩历史时，智能体把后续请求当许可而忽略规则；来源随规则交付方式、压缩策略与预算而变，针对压缩器的最强攻击可使违规翻倍以上，最强防御多数恢复规则仍会违规，保留规则也不保证遵循。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents compact long histories to fit their context windows, but the compacted context must still carry the operating rules that govern later actions. Prior work shows that violations rise after compaction, but measures compliance outside a complete agent harness and does not identify where each violation comes from. We introduce ARCBench(Agent Rule Compliance Benchmark), a configurable benchmark built on the open-source pi agent harness. Its tool-calling agent loop lets us measure rule compliance from actions taken during execution, bringing the evaluation closer to deployed agent workflows. Using ARCBench, we examine where violations after compaction come from, and how different compaction configurations and adversarial settings change their sources. We find that compaction rarely deletes the rule: most violations after compaction occur while the rule is still in the compacted history, with the agent treating a later request as permission, ignoring the rule, and proceeding anyway. Where violations come from depends on the configuration: how the rule is delivered decides whether the agent would break it even without compaction, while the compaction strategy and budget decide whether the rule survives. The strongest compactor-targeted attack more than doubles violations by corrupting the rule in the summary and changing how the agents behave, whereas the strongest defense restores the rule in most summary but still violates. Finally, retaining a rule does not guarantee compliance: compacted runs that retain the rule violate more than twice as often as runs with the full history.

papers.title_en: EvoGroup: A Self-Evolving Harness for Group Agents in Shared Contexts
papers.authors: Xinyi Xu, Xiaoyang Li, Yucheng Feng, Wenqing Chen, Youliang Yuan, Wei Shi, Rongxiang Weng, Zibin Zheng
papers.evidence: 面向共享群体上下文的自进化智能体记忆系统
papers.tldr: 面向长期团队协作的 Group Agent 需在持续累积的共享上下文中工作，但现有记忆系统多为单用户设计，难以捕捉群体关系与协作知识，手工策略也难以适应多变场景。EvoG 从六工具冷启动出发，用置信度与任务结果筛选轨迹，并对低置信情形做自我反思，再由分析代理渐进披露、分桶归纳来驱动 Harness 演化。在 EverMemBench 留出集上 pass@1 从 71.07% 提升到 89.58%，超过 Claude Code 的 85.83%；冻结后迁移到未见过的 GroupMemBench 仍优于记忆基线与人工设计 Harness。
papers.abstract_en: With the rise of Group Agent such as Claude Tag, agents increasingly serve as digital workers for long-term team collaboration. These agents operate over shared contexts that continuously accumulate through multi-user interactions. However, existing agent memory systems are mainly designed for individual users and struggle to capture group-level knowledge in shared contexts, including group relationships and collaboratively formed knowledge. Manual memory strategies further limit adaptation to diverse and evolving shared contexts. To this end, we propose \textbf{EvoGroup (EvoG)}, a self-evolving harness for group agents that starts from a minimal six-tool cold start and adapts through interaction with shared context. EvoG uses confidence and task outcomes to select informative trajectories, while also eliciting self-reflections on uncertainty in low-confidence cases. The analysis agent then examines selected trajectories through adaptive progressive disclosure, followed by bucketed analysis to synthesize high-level findings that guide the evolve agent in revising the Harness. Empirically, pass@1 on held-out split of EverMemBench improves from 71.07\% to 89.58\%, surpassing both self-evolving memory and human-designed harnesses, including Claude Code (85.83\%). To evaluate generalization, we freeze the evolved harness and evaluate it on the unseen GroupMemBench, where, with GPT-5.5, it demonstrates effective generalization and outperforms both memory baselines and human-designed harnesses.

papers.title_en: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory
papers.authors: Chih-Hsuan Yang, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Feng Yan, Rajeev Thakur
papers.evidence: 衡量长期智能体记忆的任务条件效用
papers.tldr: 长期记忆对某任务是否有用并不固定，单一重要性评分难以刻画。作者让任务盲写入器先存记忆，冻结读者在相同填充下分别带记忆与不带记忆答题，并记录形成、存储和暴露成本。在LongMemEval-V2事实回忆任务上，含答案信息的记忆带来显著配对增益（+0.33），而通用检索常漏掉这些记忆。研究据此主张按任务效用与成本共同评估记忆压缩，并发布配对测量数据集。
papers.abstract_en: A stored experience may answer one future question and offer little help with another. We measure this task-conditioned utility rather than assigning each memory a single importance score. A task-blind writer stores a memory without seeing the later task; a frozen reader then answers that task with and without the memory, using identical filler. A cost ledger records the resources used to form, store and expose the memory.   On single-call factual-recall tasks built from LongMemEval-V2 web-agent memories, the same memory helps more when it contains information needed for the answer. Its mean paired reward gain on these answer-bearing task pairs exceeds that on matched-control pairs by $+0.33$ (95% interval $+0.21$ to $+0.46$). The tested task-blind summaries and structured records yield smaller gains than Raw, including at fixed total context; a budget sweep is consistent with retention of answer-bearing content contributing to the difference. The bearing--control contrast remains positive in a new session with randomized memory position and under a second reader, although individual memory--task labels change. Generic retrieval performs above chance but misses most screen-defined answer-bearing memories. The factual-recall gains do not extend to the tested software-engineering and scientific-coding benchmarks, where even raw memories have no measurable effect. We provide a public, versioned Conditional Memory Utility Dataset of paired measurements and costs. The practical takeaway is to evaluate memory compression by the task utility it preserves alongside its costs. Task-conditioned measurements make this comparison possible; their stability must also be checked.

papers.title_en: From Benchmarks to Behaviors: A Framework for Auditing AI Agents
papers.evidence: 审计与评估AI智能体行为的框架
papers.tldr: 生成式AI日益介入信息获取，但其行为受工具、指令与用户记忆影响，研究者难以观察和控制。作者提出TRACE框架，基于开源智能体运行环境，可受控操纵系统组件并记录输入输出与执行过程。以2026年美国中期选举问答为例，发现用户记忆能显著改变引用来源选择。该工作将算法审计扩展到智能体运行框架，提供透明研究路径。
papers.abstract_en: Generative AI systems increasingly mediate access to information. Their behavior depends on tools, instructions, and user memories that are often difficult for researchers to observe or control. Here, I introduce TRACE (Transparent Research on Agent Contexts and Environments), a framework for systematically auditing how these components shape AI agent behavior. Built on an open-source agent harness, TRACE enables controlled manipulation of system components. It also records inputs, outputs, and task execution for downstream analysis. I demonstrate this framework through an experiment examining how user memories influence source selection when agents answer questions about the 2026 U.S. midterm elections. I find that memories expressing explicit preference for a publisher increase its inclusion among the first three cited sources in a response by 33-39 percentage points. Memories identifying the user as a Republican or expressing distrust of mainstream media shift citations rightward. That same media distrust memory also increases citation of sources expressing misinformation or conspiracy theories by 6.3 percentage points, with substantial variation across models. These findings demonstrate that concise user memories can alter source selection in consequential settings, even when questions and search results remain fixed. TRACE extends algorithm auditing to agent harnesses, providing a transparent way to study agent behaviors that benchmarks or commercial interfaces may struggle to isolate.

papers.title_en: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis
papers.authors: Peizhi Niu, Ge Shi, Vaibhav Gorde, Sarthak Ghosh, Christos Faloutsos, Min Cheng, Kevin Chen
papers.evidence: 将执行轨迹蒸馏为持久化 wiki 页面的智能体程序性记忆
papers.tldr: LLM智能体难以自动执行复杂企业流程，静态预建执行框架无法覆盖专有策略与状态相关恢复路径。WASP-Mem将执行轨迹与反馈蒸馏为持久互联的wiki页面，形成可复用程序记忆并支持持续学习。在TheAgentCompany上，其检查点通过率较最强基线提升4.6-6.1%，存储需求降低57-61%。研究进一步表明应让智能体组织程序记忆，把人力投入诊断环节。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents struggle to automate complex enterprise procedures because static, pre-built harness cannot capture proprietary policies, undocumented behaviors, or state-dependent recovery paths that surface only during execution. Procedural memory accrued from agent experience offers a training-free path to closing this gap -- yet unlike episodic records or semantic facts, it must consolidate repeated successes and diagnosed failures into reusable actions and recovery strategies. We introduce WASP-Mem (Wiki-based Agent-Synthesized Procedural Memory), a nimble but effective method that distills execution traces and feedback into persistent, interlinked wiki pages, enabling continual agent learning. On TheAgentCompany benchmark, WASP-Mem raises the checkpoint pass rate by 4.6-6.1% over the strongest baseline we compared across three models while requiring 57-61% less storage. We further present a systematic controlled study spanning consolidation method, feedback type, trace ingestion scope, and refinement rounds. Our results reveal that prescriptive knowledge organization such as human defined schemas and explicit deduplication rules hurts performance rather than closing the procedural-knowledge gap. In contrast, human diagnosis converts failed traces into corrective knowledge and drives sustained improvement: a single round of human diagnosis outperforms four rounds of self-judgment by 7.0-10.9%. These findings point to a simple division of labor: let agents organize procedural memory, and invest human effort where it matters most -- diagnosis.

papers.title_en: EvoRec: A Unified Self-Evolving Agentic Recommender with Dynamic Reflection Trees
papers.authors: Mengting Li, Long Zhang, Hao Jiang, Sheng Yu, Fei Pan, Peng Jiang
papers.evidence: 使用长短期与工作记忆并选择检索工具的智能体框架
papers.tldr: 传统推荐依赖固定级联管道，难以适应用户需求与反馈变化；现有agentic推荐缺少端到端决策控制和系统化失败反思。EvoRec以需求推断、规划执行和动态反思树构成统一自进化框架，通过回放验证修复并蒸馏跨用户策略，无需更新参数。在快手本地服务广告数据上Hit@50提升15.7%，七天线上A/B测试广告收入增4.6%、CTCVR增3.5%。这表明反思驱动的自进化可在工业级推荐中持续提升效果。
papers.abstract_en: Conventional recommender systems rely on fixed cascaded pipelines, limiting their ability to adapt to evolving user needs and feedback. Existing agentic recommenders introduce reasoning and tool use but often lack end-to-end decision control and systematic failure reflection. We propose EvoRec, a unified agentic recommendation framework that combines autonomous decision-making with reflection-driven self-evolution. A Need Agent infers user needs from long-term, short-term, and working memory. A Planning Agent adaptively allocates retrieval budgets between Behavior Continuation and Need Satisfaction, selects retrieval tools, and sets ranking-fusion weights. An Acting Executor executes the plan and records decision traces. Following user feedback, a Dynamic Reflection Tree identifies failures in need inference, planning, or previous repairs, proposes personalized corrections, and validates them through replay. Verified repairs update working memory and are distilled into reusable cross-user strategies, enabling continual improvement without parameter updates. Experiments on a Kuaishou local-services advertising dataset show a 15.7% Hit@50 improvement over the strongest baseline. Hierarchical reflection further improves Hit@50 by 13.1% among users with prior repairs. In a seven-day online A/B test, nearline EvoRec increases advertising revenue by 4.6% and CTCVR by 3.5%, with a 14.5% revenue gain for high-intent users. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of reflection-driven self-evolution in industrial-scale recommendation.

papers.title_en: Agent Memory as Rate-Limited Filtering: Explicit State Outlasts Long Context Beyond a Reader-Dependent Horizon
papers.evidence: 研究显式状态与长上下文作为智能体记忆在历史增长下的表现
papers.tldr: 长上下文模型读取完整访问日志时，事件一多准确率明显下降；论文将智能体记忆视为受容量限制的递归滤波，用显式状态按策略更新。在授权、撤回、过期等可执行基准上，显式状态在256事件达80-89%，优于检索、模型账本、StateMem与Mem0。推理模型读状态达96/98%，120B读长上下文在256/512事件落后4/7点、1024约10点，说明优势存在随读者变化的时间视野。贡献是给出状态依赖选择与容量遗忘的可预测框架。
papers.abstract_en: Can a language model that reads the full history of an access log say whether a service may act now? On an executable benchmark of grants, withdrawals, reinstatements, expiries, groups and change windows under a known policy, scored on pairs of histories that differ only in the order or one field of the deciding events, open models of 7 to 32 billion parameters fall from 72 to 86 percent after eight or sixteen events to 48 to 55 percent after 256, while reasoning-trained 32B models reading the current state reach 96 and 98 percent. A reasoning model of 120 billion parameters trails the state by four and seven points at 256 and 512 events and by about ten at 1,024, so the length beyond which explicit state outlasts long context grows with the reader. We treat agent memory as recursive filtering. The decision depends on the history only through a state whose size is set by the number of tracked keys. A store holding fewer component records than the state forgets on a time scale set by its capacity, and a reader model predicts its accuracy within 0.02 on average in a registered test. Retaining log lines without regard to time order errs with probability approaching one half, a bound that is attained. A filter in which a model parses each line and an explicit rule applies the updates answers 80 to 89 percent at 256 events and beats relevance retrieval, model-kept ledgers, a reimplementation of StateMem and the Mem0 library. A retriever that selects at query time the lines the queried state depends on matches it at 256 events on the first domain, so what decides is selection by the state's dependencies, which the filter performs when writing, without the query. Applying parsed updates themselves, the models fall to 58 and 59 percent. A frozen replication on a second domain with fresh wording reproduces the horizon.

papers.title_en: AttentionIndex: Accelerating Learned Sparse Attention with a Causal Inverted-File Index
papers.evidence: 按相似度分组的倒排索引与候选精化
papers.tldr: 学习型稀疏注意力由轻量索引器为每个查询从前缀中选k个键，但百万token时全量打分占用过半预填充时间。AttentionIndex构建因果倒排文件索引，按键相似度聚类并路由查询，再用原生索引器分数精排候选；索引在预填充中增量维护，查询仅访问自身前缀的簇。在GLM-5.3与DeepSeek-V4-Flash上，其预填充吞吐达穷举选择的1.3-1.8倍，并在接近HiSA吞吐时恢复更多top-k、提升长上下文准确率。
papers.abstract_en: Learned sparse attention, used in production models such as DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5, lets each query attend to only k keys chosen by a lightweight indexer, but the indexer still scores every key in the prefix. At one million tokens, this selection takes more than half of prefill time. Two-stage selection over contiguous blocks, as in HiSA, reduces this cost, but its recall declines as context grows at a fixed candidate budget. We present AttentionIndex, which routes each query over an inverted-file index that groups indexer keys by similarity and refines the candidates with the native indexer score. AttentionIndex builds the index during prefill, making new keys searchable immediately, reusing previous clustering to keep maintenance cheap, and exposing each query only to clusters built from its own prefix. On GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash at one million tokens, AttentionIndex delivers 1.3-1.8 times the prefill throughput of exhaustive selection, and at throughput within 5% of HiSA, it recovers 17.0 and 10.0 percentage points more of the exhaustive top-k, respectively. AttentionIndex also improves accuracy on long-context benchmarks by up to 18.4 percentage points over HiSA at the same candidate budget.

papers.title_en: EEFA: A Framework for the Ethical Evaluation of AI Agents
papers.evidence: 综述十二个AI智能体基准并提出评估框架
papers.tldr: 自主AI代理在医疗、法律、金融等高风险领域快速部署，但现有评测基准只测“能做什么”，忽视自主性、伤害规避、透明、隐私与问责等伦理维度。本文提出EEFA框架，含五大维度并给出可复现验证协议与测试场景。框架对齐EU AI Act和NIST AI RMF，可作为开发者、审计者和监管者的合规评估工具。贡献在于把伦理评估操作化，但实证应用仍待未来工作。
papers.abstract_en: The rapid deployment of autonomous AI agents across consequential domains including healthcare, legal services, nancial management, and enterprise workows has created an urgent governance challenge. While the eld of AI evaluation has produced sophisticated benchmarks for measuring agent capability, these frameworks measure exclusively what agents can do rather than how they do it. The ethical dimensions most critical to responsible agent deployment, in- cluding respect for human autonomy, harm avoidance, transparency and non-deception, privacy compliance, and accountability, are systematically absent from current evaluation practice. This paper addresses that gap through three contributions. First, a structured literature review of twelve leading AI agent benchmarks characterizes the ethical dimensions those bench- marks do and do not measure. Second, the Ethical Evaluation Framework for AI Agents (EEFA) is introduced as a comprehensive, operationalizable instrument for ethical agent evaluation, grounded in established AI ethics principles and designed for use by developers, auditors, and regulators. Third, a reproducible validation protocol is specied for applying the EEFA to deployed agent systems, with illustrative test scenarios across all ve framework dimensions. The EEFA is organized across ve primary dimensions: Autonomy Preservation, Harm Avoid- ance, Transparency and Non-Deception, Privacy Compliance, and Accountability and Traceabil- ity. The framework maps directly onto the requirements of the EU AI Act and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, positioning it as a practical compliance assessment instrument for high-risk AI applications. Empirical application of the framework across diverse benchmarks and agent systems is identied as a priority direction for future work.

papers.title_en: Enhancing Stock Market Information Retrieval with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.authors: Huan Phong Thai, Thu Anh Ngoc Le, Nhu Huynh Thi Le, Nhan Huu Tran, Lenh Cong Phan Pham, Hong Nhung Nguyen
papers.evidence: 面向金融知识密集型检索的检索增强生成系统
papers.tldr: 传统金融NLP系统在动态股市环境中难以保持上下文准确，回答相关性也受限。本文构建面向股市信息的检索增强生成（RAG）系统，将检索与生成结合，以提升金融文本生成的准确性和相关性。在100条股市查询数据集上，系统取得较高ROUGE-1、ROUGE-2和ROUGE-L分数，平均响应时间为1.16秒。结果表明该RAG系统能提供准确且及时的股市洞察，为金融信息检索提供了有前景的方案。
papers.abstract_en: Natural Language Processing (NLP) has been widely applied in financial domains, enabling automated analysis and retrieval of stock market information. However, traditional NLP-based systems often struggle with maintaining contextual accuracy and generating relevant responses in dynamic financial environments. To address these challenges, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) models have emerged as a powerful solution, combining retrieval-based methods with generative capabilities to enhance response quality. In this study, we present a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system designed to generate responses related to stock market information. The system integrates retrieval-based and generative approaches to enhance the accuracy and relevance of financial text generation. To evaluate its effectiveness, we employ the ROUGE metric, specifically ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L, to measure lexical and structural similarity between generated and reference texts. Experimental results on a dataset of 100 stock market-related queries demonstrate high ROUGE scores, indicating strong alignment with reference documents. Additionally, we assess latency to evaluate the system responsiveness, achieving an average response time of 1.16 seconds. These findings confirm that our RAG model is capable of providing accurate and timely stock market insights, making it a promising approach for financial information retrieval.

papers.title_en: VisSearch-Bench: Evaluating Long Horizon Visual Search in Multimodal Agents
papers.authors: ZhengXian Wu, Qianhao Nie, Zhuohong Chen, Junjie Gao, Yuyao Zhang, Yunyao Yu, Hangrui Xu, Cheng Cheng, Guiyu Ma, Jin Zhang, Xingzhong Xu, Kai Yang, Haoqian Wang
papers.evidence: 评测多模态智能体长程搜索能力的基准
papers.tldr: 多模态智能体常借助图像与网络工具完成搜索，但现有任务多将图像仅用于识别初始实体，难以考察跨图像、对象与搜索步骤的视觉上下文管理。为此，作者提出 VisSearch-Bench，包含204个人工编写任务、7大领域25个子域，覆盖集合式、序列式、混合宽深、竞争消歧和视觉结构引导搜索五类场景，并提供参考答案、可追溯证据与评分规则。评测16个多模态模型，最佳系统即使配备搜索工具也仅完全解决26.47%任务。该基准揭示连接视觉证据与搜索结果、形成完整答案仍是关键挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal agents use web and image tools to answer questions beyond their internal knowledge. Some search tasks use images mainly to identify an initial entity, then rely on text retrieval. These tasks offer limited insight into how agents connect information across images, objects, and search steps. We therefore focus on visual context management. This involves organizing and using visual information and linking it to other findings during search. Visually intensive tasks require agents to combine object appearance, local details, or spatial relations with external information. We introduce VisSearch-Bench, with 204 human-written tasks across 7 main domains and 25 subdomains. It covers Set-wise Visual Search, Sequential Visual Search, Hybrid Wide-Deep Search, Competitive Visual Disambiguation, and Visual-Structure-Guided Search. Each task provides a reference answer, traceable evidence, and scoring rules. Accuracy measures complete task success, while Process Score measures the correctness and completeness of individual results and subquestion answers. Across 16 multimodal models, the best system fully solves only 26.47% of tasks, even with search tools. These results highlight the challenge of linking visual evidence with search results to produce complete answers.
